reviewer: Claude Sonnet 5 visual inspection, not human approval
scope: All eight directions inspected per piece via games/lantern_path/proof/contact_sheet.png; not final export/animation approval.
reason: 5/5 pieces clean or acceptable after two rounds of design-doc-level fixes. lantern_piece and score_lantern_icon originally defaulted (via SDXL's own prior for 'paper lantern') to a thin wire bail handle that TripoSR could not reconstruct at 64px, producing a dark noisy tangle; fixed by adding 'no handle, solid rounded closed top' to short_desc -- lantern_piece is now clean, score_lantern_icon still carries a minor thin-line artifact on some frames but is legible and not blocker-flagged. firefly_token originally described insect anatomy ('tiny folded wings'); SDXL rendered full legs/antennae/wing-venation regardless of added negative clauses (diffusion models don't reliably obey 'no X' phrasing) and hit the same speckle blocker as this repo's known wicker-basket/glossy-apple cases; fixed by dropping the literal creature noun entirely and describing it as an abstract glowing bead, per short_desc's own documented contract (physical appearance only, game meaning belongs in name/role). altar_piece's original 'flat carved top' prompt produced a cluttered multi-part pedestal with noisy legs/base across all 8 directions (not blocker-flagged, but visually rough); fixed by simplifying to one solid rectangular block with a carved top mark, no separate base. moss_stone needed no changes and is the cleanest piece in the set.

rejected.f4435b9bb0fed01abbe3: firefly_token v1: short_desc said 'tiny folded wings'; TripoSR speckle-blocked on 6/8 frames (11-15%), same class as basket/apple fine-detail failures.
rejected.6b25b0a34dd0fe806d43: firefly_token v2: short_desc added 'no legs or wings or antennae' but kept 'firefly'; SDXL still rendered a detailed insect (legs, antennae, wing venation) and speckle-blocked again on 6/8 frames -- negative clauses did not override the noun's prior.
rejected.03b1a82c5fac2f4dd9c0: altar_piece v1: 'flat carved top' produced a cluttered pedestal with noisy legs/base on all 8 directions; never speckle-blocked but visually the roughest piece in the set, superseded by a simpler one-block redesign.
